turns.prompt_text: Jesus Christ said at some point something about healing people He had the ability to heal people And he would say is better for your story for you not to be healed Or something along those lines?
turns.response_html:
Jesus does not say that it is "better for your story not to be healed." Throughout the Gospels, whenever individuals come directly to Jesus seeking physical healing, he heals them.

However, a few well-known New Testament passages touch on very similar themes and are likely what you are thinking of:

  • The Man Born Blind (John 9:1–3): When the disciples ask if a man was born blind because of his own sin or his parents' sin, Jesus responds that neither sinned, "but this happened so that the works of God might be displayed in him." Jesus then immediately heals his sight.
  • The Death and Raising of Lazarus (John 11:4, 14–15): When Jesus hears Lazarus is sick, he delays going to see him, explaining that the illness is "for God’s glory so that God’s Son may be glorified through it" and tells the disciples he is glad he was not there initially so that their faith would grow when he raises Lazarus.
  • Paul's "Thorn in the Flesh" (2 Corinthians 12:7–9): The Apostle Paul writes that he pleaded with the Lord three times to remove a persistent physical affliction or trial. The Lord answered: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." This is the closest biblical instance where God deliberately leaves someone unhealed for the sake of a greater spiritual purpose.
  • "Better to Enter Life Maimed" (Mark 9:43–47): In a different context regarding sin and radical devotion, Jesus uses hyperbole, stating it is better to enter eternal life crippled or blind than to have two hands or eyes and be cast into hell.
